findings.title: In-process CdpRelay.stop() leaves a pid-valid relay.json and an armed browser gate — tools advertised against a dead relay
findings.failure_scenario: User opens the Browser screen and taps Stop (BrowserRelayModule.stop -> CdpRelay.stop). stop() only sets running=false and closes the accept ServerSocket: it never deletes/updates <home>/browser/relay.json (still holding pid=myPid, port, token), never terminates live WS pump tunnels, never resets the Python gate. The app pid is unchanged, so hermes_boot._arm_browser_gate_from_relay_file (hermes_boot.py:182 'if _port>0 and _token and _pid == os.getpid()') considers the file LIVE and arms BROWSER_CDP_URL+MOCH_BROWSER_RELAY on the next boot re-check or pre-serve re-arm (gateway_server.py:146-153), and browser_gate._STATE.active stays True. A new chat then gets browser_* tools whose every call dials 127.0.0.1:9334 -> connection refused / 'relay is not running'.
evidence: CdpRelay.kt:127-132 — stop() body: running.set(false), server.close, nothing else
CdpRelay.kt:176-188 — writeStateFile writes pid=myPid; nothing removes the file
hermes_boot.py:180-184 — arming condition is pid == os.getpid(), which still holds after an in-process stop
browser_gate.py:31-38 — activate() sets active=True; no deactivate path exists anywhere
reproduction_steps: Open Browser screen, start relay (relay.json now has live pid)
Tap the relay Stop control (src/lib/browserRelay.ts:121 -> BrowserRelayModule.stop)
Start a new chat and ask the agent to browse — tools are in the kit (gate still armed) but every call fails against the dead port
findings.suggested_remediation: In CdpRelay.stop(): delete relay.json (or rewrite with pid:0), close any live tunnel sockets, and call moch.browser_gate deactivate/status reset via Python when started.
findings.limitations: Not device-verified; fully traced statically. BUG-105's pid-gate fix closed only the cross-process (stale-after-restart) half; the same-process stop half remains.

findings.title: Always-on runtime runs as a dataSync foreground service with no onTimeout handling — 6-hour hard limit on Android 15+ devices
findings.failure_scenario: Manifest declares HermesService with android:foregroundServiceType="dataSync" (AndroidManifest.xml:39) and onStartCommand promotes it with FOREGROUND_SERVICE_TYPE_DATA_SYNC. On devices running Android 15 (API 35)+, dataSync FGS instances are capped at 6 hours per 24h: the system calls Service.onTimeout(int), and if the service does not stop itself the system throws ForegroundServiceDidNotStopInTimeException (process crash) after the grace period. HermesService has no onTimeout override, no type rotation, and the whole product premise ('Mochi is awake on this phone', START_STICKY automations) dies ~6h into every heavy day on those devices — taking the embedded gateway, cron-knocks watcher and FleetTurnQueue with it.
evidence: AndroidManifest.xml:39 — <service ... foregroundServiceType="dataSync"/>
HermesService.kt:207-208 — startForeground(NOTIFICATION_ID, notification, FOREGROUND_SERVICE_TYPE_DATA_SYNC)
HermesService.kt — grep: no onTimeout(short/int) override anywhere under app/android/app/src/main
reproduction_steps: On an Android 15+ device, keep the app alive with the foreground service across >6h cumulative runtime in a 24h window
Observe onTimeout -> unhandled -> ForegroundServiceDidNotStopInTimeException (logcat) and runtime death
findings.suggested_remediation: Override onTimeout(int) to stopSelf cleanly (and notify/persist), or move to a type without the 6h cap that Moch legitimately qualifies for (e.g. specialUse with a justification).
findings.limitations: Docs/platform-behavior-based (Android 15 dataSync 6h limit), not reproduced on hardware here; applies only when running on API 35+ devices regardless of targetSdk.

findings.title: HermesRuntime boot chain is single-shot and single-try: any gateway failure silently disables cron knocks for the whole process life
findings.failure_scenario: HermesRuntime.start() guards with bootAttempted.compareAndSet(false,true) and runs selftest -> hermes_boot.boot -> gateway_server.start -> cron_knocks.start inside ONE try/catch that only logs. gateway_server.start blocks up to 90s waiting for the port and can raise (port 9119 occupied, start_server import failure, uvicorn bind error). If it raises — or if anything between selftest and cron_knocks throws — the catch logs 'python boot failed' and cron_knocks.start is never reached; bootAttempted stays true so no retry is possible until process death. Result: every automation completion is silent forever — the exact 'no knock' failure class the watcher was built for, with nothing in the UI distinguishing it.
evidence: HermesRuntime.kt:28 — bootAttempted.compareAndSet(false, true) one-shot
HermesRuntime.kt:38-43 — gateway start precedes cron_knocks.start in the same try block
gateway_server.py:44-49,161-206 — start() waits up to _READY_TIMEOUT_S=90s; _port_accepts can race a foreign listener on the fixed port 9119
reproduction_steps: Hold 127.0.0.1:9119 open (or make start_server throw) before the app boots
Launch app; logcat shows 'python boot failed' once
Create an automation and let it run — it completes with no notification, permanently (until full process restart)
findings.suggested_remediation: Arm cron_knocks FIRST (it is independent of the gateway), and/or put each stage in its own try/catch; consider resetting bootAttempted on gateway failure so a later getGateway() can retry start().
findings.limitations: Failure precondition is environment-dependent; the ordering fragility itself is unconditional.

findings.title: gateway_server never sets _STATE['starting']=True — getGateway reports running=false during the entire cold boot
findings.failure_scenario: _STATE is initialized with starting:False and no code path ever sets it True. During the up-to-90s cold boot inside start(), info() returns running = started or starting = False, so the RN client polling getGateway() (mochiRuntime.ts:68) sees a not-running runtime that is actually mid-import, and connection attempts during that window fail with no 'starting' signal to key UI state or retry logic on.
evidence: gateway_server.py:33 — {"started": False, "starting": False, ...}
gateway_server.py:178-206 — start() spawns the thread and only ever writes starting:False
gateway_server.py:209-220 — info(): running = started or bool(_STATE["starting"])
reproduction_steps: Cold-start the app and poll getGateway() during the first minute: running=false while the gateway thread is importing/binding
findings.suggested_remediation: Set _STATE['starting']=True (under _LOCK) before spawning the thread in start().

findings.title: docs/install.sh is ~400 lines behind canonical moch-link/install.sh — the published copy ships no push knocks at all
findings.failure_scenario: The published installer embeds a stale moch-link-proxy: it is missing the entire v2 notification layer of the canonical script (Expo push registration via ?push=, the passive server->client WS frame watcher for approval/clarify/sudo/secret and message.complete, push receipts checking, the no-phone-attached session mirror), and its env file omits LINK_HOME (moch-link/install.sh:932-933 writes it; docs copy does not), which the canonical proxy requires as its cwd/token-file base. A user who installs from the docs URL gets a relay that connects chat but never knocks the phone on approvals or turn completions.
evidence: diff moch-link/install.sh docs/install.sh — ~400 differing lines; docs copy lacks http/https imports, LINK_HOME, registerPushToken, sendPush, checkReceipts, makeTextFrameReader, watcher v2, ?push= capture
moch-link/install.sh:932-933 vs docs/install.sh:498-499 — env file LINK_HOME line absent in docs copy
docs/install.sh:491 — 'up.on(data)' pipes bytes with no watcher feed
reproduction_steps: bash <(curl ...docs/install.sh) on a fresh machine; pair; trigger an approval — no push arrives, no push-token file is ever written
findings.suggested_remediation: Regenerate docs/install.sh from moch-link/install.sh and add a CI check (diff or hash) so the published copy cannot drift again.
findings.limitations: Static diff only; did not runtime-test either installer.

findings.title: Setup wizard offers Debian 12 but its pinned rootfs URL is dead (misspelled GitHub org) — provisioning always fails for that choice
findings.failure_scenario: ROOTFS_URLS['debian-12'] points at github.com/debuerreumaker/docker-debian-artifacts (the real org is 'debuerreotype'); the code comment itself admits 'this URL is DEAD (HTTP 404...)' and defers the fix. Meanwhile app/app/setup.tsx:122 still offers 'Debian 12 — smaller base, rock solid' in the wizard. Choosing it makes bootstrap() fail at the rootfs download step — a user-facing dead option shipped in release.
evidence: linux_env.py:58 — 'debuerreumaker' org in ROOTFS_URLS['debian-12']
linux_env.py:53-57 — comment: 'this URL is DEAD (HTTP 404 ...) fix is a tracked follow-up'
app/app/setup.tsx:122 — { id: 'debian-12', name: 'Debian 12', ... } offered in the wizard
bugs.md — no BUG entry mentions debian (grep: 0 hits)
reproduction_steps: Run setup wizard -> choose Debian 12 -> download fails 404; wizard shows install failed
findings.suggested_remediation: Correct the org to debuerreotype (dist-arm64v8 branch) or hide the debian-12 row until verified.
findings.limitations: URL liveness is from the code's own on-device 404 note; not re-verified from this sandbox (no network per audit rules).

findings.title: linux_session.run timeout desynchronizes the persistent guest shell (orphaned sentinel/rc lines poison the next command)
findings.failure_scenario: run() frames each command as '(cmd) ; echo SENTINEL ; echo rc'. On TimeoutError the branch returns {'ok':False,'error':'command timed out'} WITHOUT killing the shell: the previous payload keeps executing and its SENTINEL+rc lines arrive later, where the next run() reads them as the new command's output and exit code (garbage stdout, wrong exit status), and the new command is written while the old one still owns the shell. Other exception paths kill the shell for restart; the timeout path — the most likely one for long commands — does not.
evidence: linux_session.py:118 — wrapped command appends sentinel+rc after the payload
linux_session.py:141-142 — TimeoutError: return without proc.kill() (contrast :144-147 which kills on other exceptions)
linux_session.py:121-139 — next run() reads the leftover sentinel as its own
reproduction_steps: run('sleep 300', timeout_s=2) -> times out; immediately run('echo hello') -> output/exit belong to the dead command
findings.suggested_remediation: On timeout, kill and null the shell (same as the generic exception path), or drain until sentinel before the next write.
findings.limitations: In-tree callers are tests only today (terminal.py is a separate PTY path); severity held at low for that reason.

findings.title: BUG-115 confirmed NOT fixed in code: terminal Kill clears chunks but never the replay buffer — Retry repaints the dead session's scrollback
findings.failure_scenario: _close_locked() and kill() clear _state.chunks but nothing ever clears _state.replay (the 64KB reattach buffer banked by _bank()); start() clears chunks only as well. Kill -> Retry therefore serves replay() with the previous (dead) shell's last 64KB as the fresh session's initial screen — the exact tracker symptom.
evidence: terminal.py:_close_locked — no replay.clear() (chunks cleared only in kill)
terminal.py:kill — clears _state.chunks/_state.chunks_bytes only
terminal.py:replay — joins _state.replay unconditionally, gated only by 'alive'
terminal.py:start — _state.chunks.clear(), replay untouched
reproduction_steps: Terminal: produce output -> Kill -> Start/Retry -> screen shows the dead session's scrollback prepended

findings.title: BUG-129 confirmed NOT fixed in code: Settings 'Stop runtime' only stops the FGS — Python and the gateway keep serving
findings.failure_scenario: HermesBridgeModule.stop() calls HermesService.stop() which is just context.stopService(...). The Chaquopy interpreter, the loopback gateway (127.0.0.1:9119, holding the session token) and the cron-knocks watcher all live in the main app process and keep running; shutdownProcess() (the only real teardown) is reachable solely from the notification's Stop action.
evidence: HermesBridgeModule.kt:58-61 — stop -> HermesService.stop
HermesService.kt:135-137 — stop() = stopService only
HermesService.kt:143-153 — shutdownProcess (Runtime.exit) only invoked from ACTION_STOP notification path
reproduction_steps: Settings -> Stop runtime -> app stays alive; ws://127.0.0.1:9119 still accepts; process persists
findings.suggested_remediation: Route the settings stop through shutdownProcess (with user-confirmed semantics), or at minimum stop gateway serving + cron watcher in-process.

findings.title: BUG-132: all four shipped Kotlin/Python browser fixes are present, but the tracker's round-34 root cause (6-tool callable kit) is untouched anywhere in the tree
findings.failure_scenario: Verified present and mutually consistent: native relay start before Python boot (MainApplication.kt:70-75, writes pid-valid relay.json at process creation), 120x1s arm-retry loop polling Python.isStarted (BrowserRelayModule.kt:51-68), pre-serve relay.json re-arm (gateway_server.py:141-153), pid-gated boot arming + cache invalidation in browser_gate.activate (browser_gate.py:31-96). Per bugs.md round 34, however, the on-device callable kit is exactly the 6 deferred/bridge tools — no browser_*, no file/memory tools — so none of these arming paths can fix the symptom; the suspects live in hermes-src toolset selection (_get_platform_tools/_select_tool_names with an empty config.yaml).
evidence: MainApplication.kt:70-78 — native CdpRelay.start before HermesRuntime.start
BrowserRelayModule.kt:51-68 — 1sx120 arm loop
gateway_server.py:141-153 — pre-serve re-arm
bugs.md round 34 — decisive NO-SUCH-TOOL probe; kit = 6 tools
findings.suggested_remediation: Direct the next debugging session at hermes_cli/tools_config._get_platform_tools + model_tools._select_tool_names under an empty config (tracker's own next step); do not spend more effort on the Kotlin arming layer.
findings.limitations: Toolset-selection chain only entry-point-traced; definitive verdict needs the PC reproduction the tracker prescribes.

findings.title: moch-link install.sh checks node/npm but never systemctl — dies mid-install on hosts without a systemd user session
findings.failure_scenario: cmd_install validates 'command -v node'/'npm' but calls 'systemctl --user daemon-reload' unconditionally (set -e) when it becomes the serve launcher (also :967, :1091 for the proxy/tunnel units). On WSL-without-systemd, containers, or minimal servers, the script dies at daemon-reload after having already written env/unit files, leaving a half-installed state with no diagnostic.
evidence: install.sh:334-335 — only node/npm are probed
install.sh:412,967,1091 — unconditional systemctl --user calls under set -e
reproduction_steps: MOCH_LINK_NO_DETECT=1 install on a non-systemd host -> dies at daemon-reload after files were written
findings.suggested_remediation: Add 'command -v systemctl' (and a --user session probe) to the preflight with a clear die message.
